blocks.content: In this course, the console is our screen. We will not be using buttons or graphics yet — we use text.
The player reads questions and types answers. The program uses console.log() to show text and prompt() to read input. Simple, but enough to build a real game loop.
Thinking of the console as the screen gives you one simple rule: if the player needs to see it, you print it. So questions, options, and results all show up using console.log().

blocks.alt: Code sending output to the console as the player's screen
